A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with readable main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices. MATHGLANCE becomes MATHEMETRIC and GeoPeP becomes GEOMETRIC. Retained content can be matched despite substantial restructuring and additional experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training experiments, robustness analyses, and model-response case studies, including Tables 2–6 and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, training controls, alternative perception tasks, and diagnostic experiments in Tables 1–12 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The structured diagram generator, caption/conversation representations, and two-stage training approach are retained. v2 adds a LoRA-based adaptation for Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B alongside SVE-Math training (Appendix C). This extends the training procedure without introducing a new perception architecture or loss; the dataset renaming itself is not a method change.

E1.justification: The core 1,198-image, 1,609-question benchmark and its three domains remain unchanged. v2 adds actual MATH-V evaluation, previously only discussed, and substantially extends diagnostic coverage through overlapping-object counting, vertex-list grounding, and marker-referenced classification (Table 2; Appendix C). It also introduces MultiMath reasoning data into Qwen training.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v2 Table 1 adds Vision-R1, MINT-CoT, GPT-o4-mini-high, Math-PUMA-DeepSeek-Math-VL, URSA, and an author-based human reference. The reasoning comparison also expands beyond the mathematical models in v1 Table 3 to include Qwen2.5-VL, Vision-R1, and MINT-CoT in v2 Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 introduces modality-priority prompting, randomized vertex ordering, reasoning-only SFT and frozen-encoder controls, and Qwen training configurations using additional MultiMath data. Appendix C specifies a new 200-image overlapping-counting evaluation with three annotators, alternative acceptable answers, and free-form matching, plus a separate 200-diagram marker experiment. These are substantial new evaluation designs, rather than merely disclosed settings for retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original noise, distractor, object-count, and alignment-data analyses while adding tests of explicit modality priority, vertex-order sensitivity, overlapping counting, symbolic versus coordinate grounding, and vertex-count shortcuts. Table 8 additionally isolates the effects of perception data and visual-encoder updating. Appendix Figure 18 adds Qwen/GPT-4o reasoning cases, and some earlier error examples are replaced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or significance tests. v2's three-author annotation procedure defines acceptable counting answers; it does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new comparators, Qwen-trained variants, MATH-V, and diagnostic controls. It also revises retained entries: SVE-Math-DeepSeek+ plane relationship accuracy changes from 97.5 in v1 Table 2 to 96.5 in v2 Table 1; its conflicting-text score changes from 74.0 in v1 Table 5 to 82.5 in v2 Table 4. These are reported-value revisions, not established same-setting gains from rerunning experiments.

T1.justification: A local mathematical correction appears in the retained worked response: v1 Figure 16(b) says the central angle is half the inscribed angle, whereas v2 Figure 17(b) correctly states the reverse relationship. The displayed equation was already correct. Neither version develops a broader theoretical analysis or formal proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a perception benchmark, structured geometric training data, and evidence connecting perception with reasoning. v2 adds vertex-order insensitivity as a headline diagnostic finding and explicitly extends its transfer claims to generic 7B/32B models. Its abstract also makes the claim about improvements without additional chain-of-thought data more explicit.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning persistent textual reliance despite visual-priority prompts, failure to internalize vertex-order constraints, and possible reasoning-data overfitting. Appendix J substantially expands the limitations beyond v1's brief future-work remarks: synthetic geometry may not represent textbooks, handwriting, or scans; OCR and marker recognition remain uncovered; and visual grounding is not explicitly interleaved with reasoning. It also qualifies that better perception does not guarantee reliable reasoning.

D1.justification: v1 mainly supplies inference settings. v2 Appendix C adds trainable-module descriptions, batch sizes, learning rates, optimizer and schedule, precision, distributed-training setup, GPU configurations, and runtimes. It updates the project-page pointer and documents licensing and planned data/code release. However, v1's explicit 200K training-set composition and 512×512 evaluation-resolution statement disappear; this does not establish changes to the underlying data quantities or resolution.

R1.justification: The original related-work discussion is largely retained, but v2 substantially expands methodological positioning in Section 3.2 and Appendix C. It contrasts perception training with MINT-CoT's interleaved visual reasoning and Vision-R1's reinforcement-learning approach, discussing complementary scope and different data requirements. It also adds citations to texture-bias research, Math-PUMA, and URSA.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and terminology, substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, and reorganizes the benchmark section. Detailed construction moves from the main text to Appendix F, and dataset statistics move to Appendix B. The contribution-list presentation is replaced by a revised diagnostic narrative, with additional ethics, implementation, limitations, and disclosure sections.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column design with new headers and abstract styling. v2 expands comparison tables, adds six analysis tables and two figures, relocates the statistics display, restyles plots, and revises several illustrated examples. Many original figures remain with renumbering rather than representing new evidence.

improvement.justification: v1's transfer evidence centers on one specialized 7B model and alignment-dataset comparisons. v2 adds reasoning-only SFT and frozen-encoder controls (Table 8), tests Qwen7B/32B, and supplies substantial training details and applicability limits (Appendices C and J). These address important weaknesses in attribution, validation breadth, and reproducibility. The abstract's claim about no additional chain-of-thought data needs qualification because Qwen training adds MultiMath samples, and some cross-table inconsistencies remain. These issues limit interpretation but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
